newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila official confirms ban on constitution change.
newsitem.headline: Manila official confirms ban on constitution change.

text.p: The Philippine Supreme Court on Tuesday upheld its ban on attempts to petition for a change in the constitution to allow President Fidel Ramos to run for a second term, a court spokeswoman said.

"(The challenge to the decision is) denied with finality, the arguments therein set forth not being of sufficient cogency to persuade the requisite majority of the court to modify or reverse the (original) decision," she said in a statement.
The vote was 6-6 which meant the court's earlier decision stood to disallow the petition by a citizens group.
Political analysts said the decision by the court to keep the ban effectively wiped out the hopes of Ramos's supporters to keep him in office when his current six-year term expires next June.

Ramos has distanced himself from the group and repeatedly denied he has any plans of running for re-election in the May 1998 presidential polls. The 10-year-old constitution limits a president to only one term.
